issues.legal_issue: Compensation for delayed possession cannot be awarded arbitrarily under multiple heads for the same default when the agreement specifies the consequence of delay, absent exceptional and strong reasons.
material_facts: The buyer’s agreement specified a payment for each month of delay in handing over possession.
The consumer fora awarded compensation for the same delay through interest on the deposited amount, additional lump-sum compensation, and litigation costs.
The awards were not founded on evidence of loss or injury assessed by recognised principles, and the compensation formula was not rationally connected to the default.
issues.conclusion: The awards of compensation under multiple heads were unsustainable because they compensated the same default and were not supported by a proper foundation; the agreed consequence of delay should apply unless exceptional and strong reasons justify otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: The Consumer Protection Act, 1986 empowers consumer fora to award compensation for loss or injury, including punitive damages, but compensation cannot be arbitrary or based on a rule of thumb. Where parties have agreed on the consequence of delayed possession, that consequence governs absent exceptional and strong reasons to award more. Interest may compensate for deprivation of the use of money and may encompass the consequences of delay, as explained in Secretary, Irrigation Department, Government of Orissa v. G.C. Roy, (1992) 1 SCC 508; separate awards for the same default are not sustainable.

rule.if: possession_delay_complaint and agreement_sets_delay_consequence and same_delay_compensated_under_multiple_heads and not exceptional_reasons_for_higher_compensation

predicates.possession_delay_complaint: A consumer brings a claim concerning delayed delivery of possession of an agreed unit.
predicates.agreement_sets_delay_consequence: The parties agreed on a consequence payable for delay in delivering possession.
predicates.same_delay_compensated_under_multiple_he: The consumer forum awards more than one form of compensation for the same delay.
predicates.exceptional_reasons_for_higher_compensat: The consumer forum has a supported exceptional reason to award compensation beyond the agreed consequence.

issues.definition: When a possession-delay claim involves an agreed consequence and the same delay is compensated under multiple heads without exceptional supporting reasons, those multiple awards cannot stand.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for delayed possession in this project is to be calculated by interest from the end of the developer’s agreed possession period, with a later starting date for a transferee and interest continuing through the specified period after an offer of possession.
material_facts: The appeals concerned complaints seeking possession of units in a housing project where the developer had an available possession period of three years under the agreement.
The developer stated that the flats were complete and occupation certificates had been obtained, and the Court directed that a copy of the certificate accompany the offer of possession.
Earlier appeals concerning the same project had been resolved on terms providing for interest at nine per cent from expiry of the three-year period, or from the date of transfer if later.
The Court directed that interest at that rate continue for two months from the offer of possession in all situations, while necessary maintenance work was to be completed within those two months.
issues.conclusion: The developer was directed to pay interest as compensation for delay from expiry of the three-year period, or from the transferee’s later transfer date, and to continue payment for two months from the offer of possession.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the settlement terms in DLF Homes Panchkula Pvt. Ltd. v. Himanshu Arora and DLF Homes Panchkula (P.) Ltd. v. Sushila Devi, which provided for interest at nine per cent in possession cases after the developer’s three-year period and, for a transferee, from the later of expiry of that period or transfer. The Court also directed that interest continue for two months after the offer of possession, regardless of circumstances.

predicates.possession_claim_in_delayed_project: A consumer seeks possession of a unit in a housing project in which delivery was delayed.
predicates.possession_period_exceeded: The developer’s agreed period for delivering possession has expired.
predicates.possession_offered: The developer has made an offer of possession of the unit.
predicates.applicable_start_date: The relevant starting point is expiry of the developer’s agreed possession period, or a later transfer date where the claimant is a transferee.

issues.definition: For a delayed-possession claim in which possession is offered, interest runs from the applicable start date and continues through the post-offer period.

issues.legal_issue: A consumer compelled to pursue consumer proceedings over delayed possession is entitled to one consolidated award for non-interest claims such as mental agony and litigation expenses, but not additional amounts for those claims.
material_facts: The consumers had been forced to invoke the jurisdiction of consumer fora because of the possession disputes.
The consumer fora had awarded amounts under different heads, including mental agony and litigation expenses, in addition to interest for delayed possession.
The Court set a consolidated amount for those non-interest claims and specified that no further amount was payable over it.
issues.conclusion: The consumers were entitled to a consolidated amount on all accounts such as mental agony and litigation expenses, but no other amount over and above that consolidated award.
issues.legal_principle: Compensation under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 must be just and supported by the loss or injury suffered; multiple awards should not duplicate compensation for the same default. The Court therefore resolved the non-interest claims through a single consolidated award.

predicates.consumer_forum_proceeding: A consumer brings a complaint before a consumer forum concerning a housing transaction.
predicates.consumers_forced_to_invoke_forum: The consumers had to invoke the consumer forum’s jurisdiction to pursue their dispute.
predicates.non_interest_claims_arise_from_same_poss: Claims such as mental agony and litigation expenses arise from the same possession dispute.

issues.definition: When consumers are forced to pursue a possession dispute before a consumer forum, their related non-interest claims are limited to one consolidated award.

issues.legal_issue: Interest on a refund of amounts deposited for a housing unit is payable at the rate adopted by the Court, with a later starting date where the unit has been transferred.
material_facts: The consumers in these appeals sought refunds of amounts deposited with the developer.
The State Commission had awarded interest at fifteen per cent per annum from the respective deposit dates until repayment.
The Court considered the interest rate adopted in earlier appeals concerning the same project and reduced the rate to nine per cent.
The Court directed that, where a flat had been transferred, interest would run from the later of expiry of three years from the agreement or the transfer date.
issues.conclusion: The refund was to carry interest at nine per cent from the respective deposit dates until refund, except that for a transferred flat interest was payable from the later of expiry of three years from the agreement or the date of transfer.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the interest rate used in the earlier consent dispositions concerning the same project, including DLF Homes Panchkula Pvt. Ltd. v. Himanshu Arora and DLF Homes Panchkula (P.) Ltd. v. Sushila Devi. For a transferred flat, the Court applied the later of expiry of the three-year period from the agreement or the transfer date as the starting point.

predicates.refund_claim_consumer_proceeding: A consumer brings a consumer-forum claim seeking refund of payments made for a housing unit.
predicates.deposits_made_for_housing_unit: The consumer made deposits towards the housing unit.
predicates.refund_ordered: The adjudicating body directs repayment of the deposited amounts.
predicates.applicable_start_date: The starting point is the dates of deposit, or, if the unit was transferred, the later of expiry of the agreed three-year period and the transfer date.

issues.definition: When a consumer is awarded a refund of housing-unit deposits, interest runs until repayment from the applicable start date.
